text:
mira: quick heartbeat — want to land follow-up on variant lease semantics before friday. still seeing clients assume absolute leases

alex: yup. main mismatch is some SDKs treat `lease_ms` as authoritative while control plane treats it as hint for eviction. need a compatibility story.

sam: can we standardize on two fields: `pin.soft_ttl` (best-effort) and `pin.hard_ttl` (enforced by control plane)? that maps nicely to current behavior

li: +1. also add `pin.affinity` enum: `soft|hard|none`. soft = prefer but can evict; hard = deny eviction until hard_ttl. none = no local affinity. keeps routing simpler.

mira: proposed minimal schema snippet for client shim (examples inline):

```json
{
  "pin.affinity": "soft",
  "pin.soft_ttl": 300,
  "pin.hard_ttl": 3600,
  "rollout.variant": "v2-small-quant",
  "rollout.priority": 10,
  "rollout.compat_hints": ["kv_cache_v1"]
}
```

alex: i like the explicit keys (dot-notation) because it avoids nested parsing differences in older clients. but we should also accept nested form on the control plane for readability. control plane -> sdk mapping layer handles both

sam: operational question: how do we express transient affinity (eg canary for 5m)? `pin.soft_ttl` covers, but need an auto-extension signal if traffic persists

li: add `pin.extend_on_hit=true` optional flag. if control plane sees continuous requests and within hard_ttl, it nudges SDK to refresh lease. we should be careful about churn and DDoS amplification though

mira: telemetry fields to emit: `pin_granted`, `pin_revoked_reason`, `pin_current_affinity`, `pin_hard_expiry_iso`. we need these for rollout regressions and to debug noisy extensions

alex: agree. also emit `rollout_eval_id` so logs tie back to a specific rollout/experiment in the control plane

sam: about deprecation: mark `lease_ms` deprecated for one minor release, log warnings in SDKs, and map lease_ms -> pin.hard_ttl if present (legacy behavior). document mapping thoroughly

li: rollout metadata ordering: control plane should honor explicit `rollout.priority` first, then `rollout.compat_score` if present, then affinity. puts a clear predecence for policy code

mira: one more: fallback behavior when `pin.affinity=hard` but node capacity low. control plane should either refuse assignment (fail) or fallback to `hard->soft` policy depending on tenant policy. we should surface tenant-level override: `tenant.enforce_hard_pins=true|false`

alex: +1. default to fallback -> soft with emitted event `pin_fallback_to_soft` so ops know it happened

deploy-bot: build #platform:pin-schema updated draft at https://github.internal/r/redwood/platform/pin-schema/diff?sha=feat/lease-refactor :white_check_mark:

mira: awesome. next actions: alex to draft SDK warning PR mapping lease_ms, sam to add extend_on_hit guard rails, li to add telemetry schema, mira will update the control plane mapping and write a short migration playbook. sync tomorrow 10am

li: adding note — we should test with very short soft_ttl (<=5s) to ensure batching/caching isn't degraded. some clients might thrash

sam: yeah i'll run a small load test with soft_ttl=2s and extend_on_hit=false, then one with extend_on_hit=true

mira: cool. thanks all :thumbsup:
